about: Match the game (sun-gamebg): byte-identical in the web app, the desktop app and the server. gameKey = the comparable form of a status text / game name; pick = which game a room shows (members' shared statuses + the room's Now playing; call players first; ties -> most recent, then the smaller id); stabilise = at most one change per HOLD_MS, a candidate must last SETTLE_MS, the first look shows at once (a first look of nobody starts no hold); veil = the smallest theme-colour veil alpha (steps of 0.01 in [floor, cap]; every stronger veil up to 1 must be safe too) that keeps every text colour (those that pass on the plain theme) at the target contrast over every measured art cell (bound: every 5x5 neighbourhood's per-channel min and max, so a downscale's averages are covered).

pick.name: statuses that are not games do not count
tie goes to the most recent
people outside the room do not count
the room's now playing is one vote
two statuses beat the room's now playing
callers without a game status play the room's now playing
a call with no games falls back to the room
callers who are not members are ignored
same count and time: the smaller id
a name the server does not know is not a game
now playing that is not a game
ties compare ids as JavaScript does (UTF-16 code units)

stabilise.name: the first look shows at once
tabbing in and out does not flicker
at most one change per hold
going to nobody waits the same
starting with nobody: the first game shows after the settle (no hold)
back to the shown game resets the wait

veil.name: dark: a white sky needs more veil
dark: already dark art keeps the floor
unreachable: no veil (null = draw no art)
a text that already fails on the theme is skipped
fitted to the margin, included by the need
the margin is out of reach: the need still holds
a pixel the luminance order missed (bound cells)
every stronger veil must hold too (a fade through the theme)
averages of neighbouring pixels are bounded too (alternating red and green)

mode.name: nothing set: game art automatically
a cleared state counts as nothing set
kind game
a preset wins
a custom image wins
an explicit none turns game art off
the space's wallpaper wins over nothing set
the space asks for game art
the room's own choice beats the space
a newer version is left alone
game art switch off
show chat backgrounds off
not an object
the agreed None: kind none turns game art off
the agreed preset: kind preset wins
the agreed image: kind image wins
kind game with a fallback preset
an unknown kind is left alone
Match the game as written (no preset) shows game art
a newer kind without a preset: no game art

fit.name: desktop 1x: covering would upscale, keep 1:1 and fade the bottom
5K window: narrower than the area, fade sides and bottom
phone 3x: 1:1 device pixels, cropped at the sides

bound.name: one row: each pixel's neighbourhood min and max corners (upper with max blue, then lower with min blue)
a 2:1 downscale of alternating red and green stays inside the bound (2x3 image)

sheet.name: nothing set, nobody playing: write the game kind
nothing set, art already showing: nothing to write
already Match the game: nothing to write
already Match the game with art: nothing to write

parse.name: absent: unset (game art may show by itself)
game without a preset (what Match the game writes)
game with an effect, no preset
game with a preset and an effect
image with a bad id = its preset
a newer kind with a preset = its preset
a newer kind without a preset = plain (an old client shows no art, never broken)

ink.name: OLED: a #808080 role name on white art is measured (3-2)
OLED: the same art with no role colours (a weaker veil would do)
role colours: case folded, duplicates and unreadable entries dropped
light: a pale role name on dark art

art_size.name: one pixel over the area cap
one pixel over the side cap: no art (R5)
tall: one over the side cap
a thin strip under the area cap but over the side cap
both sides at the cap: over the area
